description: The glob-to-regex converter uses (.*) for each * wildcard. In the regex '\A(.*)foo(.*)\z', the first (.*) is greedy and will consume 'foo' if possible before backtracking. For patterns like '*foo*', the greedy (.*) causes exponential backtracking when matching long strings that partially match (e.g. 'aaaaaaaaaaafoo' followed by no second 'foo'). fancy-regex uses a backtracking engine for lookaheads/lookbehinds but falls back to RE2-like linear time for simple patterns -- however (.*) with multiple star captures can still be slow. The fix is to use lazy (.*?) for intermediate stars or to rewrite as a non-backtracking NFA. RFC 5228 §2.7.1 does not specify greedy vs lazy, but Sieve glob matching is traditionally leftmost-longest which is consistent with greedy, so this is a performance concern not a correctness one.
title: sieve: sieve_glob_to_regex_capturing uses (.*)  for star — greedy, may cause unexpected match semantics
